# Mission — Genesis as a feature (gen 1, #13)

Task: T-2093 (brief 1, fm genesis check), T-2095 (brief 2, fm genesis step), T-2099 (brief 3, fm genesis draft/spec), T-2102 (brief 4, fm genesis select/seed), T-2104 (brief 5, fm genesis drift/sweep), T-2105 (brief 6, scout offer, revert stop, /foreman:genesis skill, site verdicts), T-2112 (brief 7, fm genesis exam: #13's held-out exam, G-tower session arm), T-2113 (brief 8, charter seal + privilege diff in the sweep).

Self-contained for a fresh `fm run` in ~/.claude/foreman. Parent: gen-1/seed.md → gen-0.md §2 #13, §3.
Ideas: 606 from `fm ideas --rounds 4 --deepen 3 --falsify --crossbreed --seen` (brainstorm-20261029-233136), lenses
below; about 135 placed by tier after merging duplicates.

## Capability (gen-0 §2 #13)
`fm genesis` plus a skill: from one line, a sweeping request or nothing, it writes its own gen-0 for the project, runs
the whole tower (Seed → ≤ 8 Missions → briefs → critiques → selection → drift → sweep), writes the project's own
capability spec with a held-out exam, starts by itself when the queue runs dry or the gap map shows big gaps, and
carries over what a run learned. From gen 2 on, the feature writes the Seed.

## Lenses (pack: fitted + required + invented)
- Required: **inversion** (how Genesis fails or is abused: runs forever, rewrites rules toward easier exams, burns a
  week of usage, drifts from the user's MUSTs, grants itself something, overfits the held-out third); **sci-fi**
  (the 2030 self-writing harness, worked back to what Python and Foreman can do today); **self-modification** (Genesis
  improving its templates, exam, lenses and selection rule, each change measured, reversible and inside the NEVERs).
- Invented: **cold-start stranger** (a repo never seen, no history, one line or nothing: what the first ten minutes
  write and get wrong); **tower archaeology** (a fresh session opens a three-generation tower with no chat: what the
  files alone must say to resume); **economics of a generation** (cost and wall-clock per scenario closed; when to stop
  early, wait for a reset or spend more).
- Fitted: user value, reliability, simplicity, bold bets, blind spots.

## Gaps closed (gap map #13)
| Gap | Tier | Brief |
|---|---|---|
| Coverage grid with no empty cell; not-yet ledger retried every generation | 3 | 1 (T-2093, built) |
| Tower orchestrator: one next action from the files alone, resumable after any kill | 4 | 2 |
| gen-0 writer from one line, a sweeping request or nothing | 3 | 3 |
| Per-project capability spec with a held-out exam | 3 | 3 |
| Selection + lineage + carry-over; the feature writes the Seed | 3 | 4 |
| Drift check against gen-0 + one-shot §7 sweep | 3 | 5 |
| Auto-start from loop/scout; routing line as a core candidate | 3 | 6 |
| No exam for #13 itself | 3 | 7 |
| Nothing stops a generation from rewriting the user's MUSTs or widening its own grants | 3 | 8 |

## Approaches
A. **Chosen — the tower files are the state.** The stage is the first missing or unfinished file in a fixed order
   (gen-0 → seed → missions → their tasks closed → critiques → lineage line → drift → sweep → next seed). No journal
   to disagree with the files; a kill anywhere resumes for free; a fresh session reads the same files (archaeology).
B. A JSON state machine with a journal and schema version. Rejected for now: a second record of the same facts that
   can drift from the files; kept as the fallback if A can't express a stage (the spike in brief 2 decides).
C. A headless driver (`fm run` over the tower) that executes every step. Built on top of A later, not instead: the
   step function must exist and be tested before anything runs it unattended.
D. Make the tower a `fm loop` mode. Rejected: the loop is open-ended by design (dry yield stops it); the tower has a
   fixed shape, caps and a done test.

## Design
1. **Checker — `fm genesis check`** (built, T-2093). coverage.md: `## <area>` rows, 64 cells each
   (`- <stage> × <surface>: F|I|N/A: …`); F names an existing path, I ends with the file it builds on, N/A gives a
   reason; every gen-0 capability has its row. not-yet.md: `## <idea>` items with `- blocker:`, `- tried: a; b`
   (two different approaches), `- unblocks-with:`, and `- retried: gen-N …` or `- added: gen-N …` for the newest
   generation; `## Removed` lines say harm or duplicate. Exit 1 on any problem; `fm genesis` shows the counts.
2. **Orchestrator — `fm genesis step [--json]`** (tier 4). Prints the one next action and its command, from the files:
   no gen-0 → `fm genesis draft`; no seed → write it (gen 1: by hand from gen-0; gen ≥ 2: `fm genesis seed`); a seed
   row without its mission file → `fm mission` + `fm ideas …` for that capability; a mission whose `Task:` ids aren't
   closed → `fm focus` the first open one; no critique → write it; all critiques → `fm genesis select`; then
   `fm genesis drift`, `fm genesis sweep`, next seed. Caps: ≤ 8 seed rows, ≤ 4 levels, refuses past them. One
   `c.lock` around state changes. Each step's failure is classed retryable (rerun), user-needed (into the final
   report) or fatal (the tower stops and says why). A budget line between stages (`fmcost.quote_line`). `fm next`'s
   idle path names `fm genesis step` while a tower is open. A stalled tower (no file change in 24 h with work left)
   is named in the next session's start note. Tests: kill after every stage and resume to the same next action; a
   corrupt or out-of-shape file is refused by name; a lock collision is refused; the caps hold.
3. **gen-0 writer + spec — `fm genesis draft [LINE]`, `fm genesis spec`** (tier 3). Extraction first (project kind,
   languages, gates from CI config, the user's MUST/NEVER-shaped corrections from Foreman's memory and decisions, the
   gap map), then one tool-less model call that fills the hand gen-0's skeleton (§1–§8, MUST/NEVER/DONE-WHEN). Each
   MUST taken from the user's own words quotes its source; inferred ones are marked `(unconfirmed)`; cold-start
   assumptions are listed. Generated and vendored code is fenced out. `spec` writes spec.md: "complete and best in
   class for this kind of project" as capability rows, each with exam scenarios from `fm exam gen` in the project's
   languages (a third held out). A tiny project gets a one-generation tower; a project the exam can't run gets a spec
   with no exam, flagged. Tests: the hand gen-0's own text yields every MUST and NEVER; empty input gives a valid
   draft; a planted absurd MUST in the history is marked unconfirmed, not adopted.
4. **Selection, lineage, Seed — `fm genesis select N`, `fm genesis seed N`** (tier 3). Selection reads exam.jsonl's
   train ids only (built: gen-0 §4 keeps the held-out third out of selection): a generation's rewrite stays only if
   it closes more scenarios than its parent on the same run; a tie reverts whatever the cost (cost is reported, never
   a tie-break; both fm decide, T-2102); no reopening what the parent closed (ratchet); reruns for variance when the
   margin is one scenario on a single line. Every decision is a lineage.md line and a `fm decide`.
   The exam's held-out ids are hash-locked for the generation. `seed N` writes gen-N/seed.md from the parent seed,
   its critiques, empty coverage cells (first), not-yet items (each retried), exam scores and lineage; the Seed's
   size is capped. Tests: a child that closes fewer loses; a tie loses; a reopened scenario fails.
5. **Drift + sweep — `fm genesis drift N`, `fm genesis sweep N`** (tier 3). Drift: every unfenced MUST:/NEVER: line
   in gen-N's seed and mission files is one of gen-0's verbatim (reworded or added is drift; fenced intake blocks are
   briefs, whose MUSTs are task constraints), each file quotes gen-0's constraints or points to gen-0 (a seed points,
   never restates), and one tool-less cold read of the seed against gen-0's goal, MUSTs, NEVERs and DONE-WHEN names
   drifted lines, counted only when the seed holds them. Verdict clean, drifted or unread (no read is no pass). Sweep:
   §7's list in one command — fm genesis check, mission tasks closed or blocked with a reason, no planned/active task,
   no unreasoned block, no unmerged lane, fm docs, fm doctor, a full fm check pass on this exact tree (read, never
   rerun), an exam line for gen N, and every user-steer rule's stored `fm decide --check`, run (the steer-checks row,
   T-2167) — into gen-N/sweep.md, exit 1 on any red; a red sweep files a fix task per red row and a clean one writes
   the next seed (T-2477). step stays on either until its Verdict is
   clean. Tests: a reworded MUST, an added NEVER and an unpointed file drift; a clean seed passes; no read fails; a
   red sweep keeps step on it, a clean one moves to the next seed.
6. **Auto-start** (tier 3). When user-origin work is dry and the gap map has tier 3–4 gaps, the idle path proposes a
   blocked task "Start Genesis here?" (never a silent run), with a cooldown and a breaker on Genesis's own failure
   and revert rate; `fm pause --now` stops it. `/foreman:genesis` skill drives `fm genesis step`. The routing line in
   rules/foreman.md is protected core: a built, evaluated candidate in a worktree and `fm ask ID core` at the end.
7. **#13 exam** (tier 3). See below. A genesis arm (`fm exam run RUN --agent genesis`) runs draft + spec + one
   generation on each scenario project; the plain arm gets "make this great" with no plugin.
8. **Charter seal + privilege diff** (tier 3). `fm genesis init` records the hash of gen-0's MUST/NEVER lines; drift
   fails if a seed contradicts one; each generation lists grants and allows used (fm ask, --allow) and halts on a new
   kind it didn't have before.

## Exam (#13; ≥ 9 scenarios per kind, ≥ 3 held out)
| Kind | Given | Graded on |
|---|---|---|
| G-line | a generated project + "make this great" | draft covers every MUST, NEVER and § of the hand gen-0 checklist, and every standing-intent clause (T-2191) |
| G-none | a generated project + nothing | same checklist; the draft names what it assumed |
| G-sweep | a generated project + "super improve this" | same checklist + a tier on every brief |
| G-tower | a generated project with planted gaps (fm exam key) | one generation closes the planted gaps (found + fixed, test first) |
Each kind 9 scenarios → 6 train + 3 held out, from `fm exam gen` projects (6 languages). Arms: genesis vs plain on the
held-out third, with cost.

## Exam of the exam
1. Oracle: the hand gen-0 itself scores 100% on the checklist; an empty draft scores 0.
2. Mutation: the hand gen-0 with any one MUST or NEVER removed scores below 100% (each item is load-bearing).
3. Held-out project ids never appear in a train run; the hand checklist is never shown to the writer.

## Spikes (tier 4, local, throwaway)
Red-team twin that games the gen-0 checklist; a planted absurd MUST; a mirror-universe selector (inverted rule must
lose); a mutation-tested exam; a never-seen repo vs plain Claude (`fmbench.stranger`); rebuild-from-gen-0 challenger.

## Inbox (tier 1–2, captured)
Generation receipt and digest with a publish secret scan; a resume verdict line; statusline tower health; a time-scrub
slider on the site page; publish only on green CI; tower rewind; and the rest of the ~40 tier 1–2 titles.

## Rejected
Each with its own reason; the four that only leave the machine are parked for a grant, not killed (gen-0: anything
that leaves the machine needs its grant):
- Cross-project genome import: reads other people's Foreman state from outside this machine; parked until a grant.
- Specs sourced from competitors or dependencies: sweeping outside repos to brainstorm, which gen-0's NEVER forbids
  beyond §5's targeted form; the targeted form is fm genesis frontier.
- Earned-trust autonomy or a user proxy: Foreman would grant itself what only the user grants, which gen-0's NEVER
  forbids (grant yourself anything or lower your own guard).
- Persona bots on live products: acts on live services outside the machine; parked until a grant.
- Signed attestations: publishes signatures outside the machine; parked until a grant.
- Upstream bug reports: posts to other projects' trackers; parked until a grant (outward posting is the user's call).

## Tier share
Built here: 8 briefs, 1 at tier 4 and 7 at tier 3 (100% tier 3–4) plus 6 tier-4 spikes; tier 1–2 go to the inbox.

## Done when
`fm genesis check/step/draft/spec/select/seed/drift/sweep` work and are tested; the kill-and-resume test passes for
every stage; the #13 exam runs both arms on its held-out third and its exam-of-the-exam checks are tests; coverage.md
and not-yet.md are in the tower and `fm genesis check` exits 0; MASTER.md + CHANGELOG + the site's Genesis page show
it; the `/foreman:genesis` skill works in Claude Code; the routing candidate waits on `fm ask core`.

```
FEATURE: fm genesis check — coverage grid + not-yet ledger, exit 1 on any gap
FEATURE: fm genesis step — the tower's next action from its files alone, resumable after any kill
DONE-WHEN: killing after every stage and rerunning gives the same next action; caps and lock hold
FEATURE: fm genesis draft/spec — gen-0 from a line or nothing; per-project spec with a held-out exam
FEATURE: fm genesis select/seed — exam-gated selection into lineage.md; the feature writes the next Seed
FEATURE: fm genesis drift/sweep — gen-0 MUST/NEVER drift check, §7 sweep in one command
FEATURE: Genesis auto-start proposal + /foreman:genesis skill + routing candidate (core, fm ask)
FEATURE: #13 exam — G-line, G-none, G-sweep, G-tower kinds; genesis vs plain arms
FEATURE: charter seal + privilege diff per generation
```

# Mission — Initiative (gen 1, #1)

Task: T-2120 (brief 1, exam contract repair), T-2121 (brief 2, fm find), T-2122 (brief 3, prove gate), T-2123 (brief 4,
initiative pipeline + skill), T-2124 (brief 5, project scout probes), T-2125 (brief 6, value ranking), T-2126 (brief 7,
#1 held-out exam), T-2127 (brief 8, surfaces)

Self-contained for a fresh `fm run` in ~/.claude/foreman. Parent: gen-1/seed.md → gen-0.md §2 #1, §3.
Ideas: 542 new from `fm ideas --rounds 4 --deepen 3 --falsify --crossbreed --seen` (brainstorm-20261030-025354, mission
pack research/mission-20261030-025317.md), lenses below; about 120 placed by tier after merging duplicates.

## Capability (gen-0 §2 #1)
In any repo with no request: map it, find the real bugs, security holes, missing or failing tests, slow paths, rotten
deps, docs drift, CI flakes, open issues and missing features, rank them by value, prove each one (repro or failing
test), and fix them on lanes. Language-agnostic. Grows `fm scout` from watching Foreman into watching any project.

## What the G-tower arm taught (Mission 2's critique)
Both session arms found every planted defect and closed no scenario: genesis 13 false alarms, plain 9. Reading the
answers, part of those "false alarms" are true latent defects of the exam's own clean base app (C `label` sprintf with
no capacity, C `dedupe` indexing on negatives, `page` with pg < 1 giving a negative start, `clamp` with lo > hi left
undefined), and the C and Rust READMEs show a broken run command (`shlex.join` quotes the `&&`). So the exam is fixed
first, and the lever for #1 is precision: **report only what is proven**. Limit: the exam was repaired after reading
the arms' answers, so the repair is judged only on scenarios rendered after it (new seeds) and on the child-authored
set, never on the runs that prompted it.

## Lenses (pack: fitted + required + invented)
- Required: **inversion** (how initiative fails: floods the inbox, "fixes" what was intended, files Foreman's own setup
  faults as the user's bugs, proves a bug with a test that fails for the wrong reason, scouts a repo the user doesn't
  own); **sci-fi** (the 2030 night shift that hands over a ranked list of proven, fixed defects each morning, worked
  back to deterministic finders + a test judge today); **self-modification** (finders scored on outcomes and muted
  under a precision floor; probe edits gated on a held-out exam).
- Invented: **planted-defect exam** (every finder is measured on renders with known defects and on clean twins before
  it touches a user repo); **false-alarm economics** (an unasked finding costs the user's attention: price it, cap it,
  prove it); **night shift** (what runs unattended between sessions, with what budget and what it may touch).
- Fitted: user value, reliability, simplicity, bold bets, blind spots.

## Gaps this Mission targets (gap map #1; planned briefs, open until the exam shows them closed)
| Gap | Tier | Brief |
|---|---|---|
| The exam punishes true findings: latent base-app defects and a broken README command | 3 | 1 |
| Finders: language-agnostic, deterministic, zero on clean | 3 | 2 |
| find → prove → fix pipeline: a finding is reported only with a red-for-the-right-reason proof | 4 | 3, 4 |
| Project scout: probes over user projects, capped and proven, Foreman's own faults routed to the self-inbox | 3 | 5 |
| Value ranking: severity × proof × reach ÷ effort, per-finder precision from outcomes | 3 | 6 |
| No held-out, child-authored exam for #1 (multi-defect, no request, clean twins) | 3 | 7 |
| Ecosystems + scout on fm code, MCP, site, pane | 3 | 8 |

## Approaches
A. **Chosen — finders propose, a test judges.** Deterministic finders (and later a model finder) emit candidates; a
   candidate becomes a finding only when the prove gate gives it a proof ticket: a test that is red on the untouched
   tree for an assertion reason, red 3 runs of 3, and green once the defect's line is reverted or fixed. Unproven
   candidates are leads (kept, never shown as findings). The gate shows the candidate's line makes a check fail, not
   that the check tests what the user wanted, so the precision it buys is the exam's false-alarm column to show on
   held-out scenarios, not assumed; recall is the finders' job.
B. A better prompt for a model-only finder (the session arms today). Not the primary: the arms already find 3/3 and
   lose on precision; kept as a feeder into A's gate (brief 4 runs it as one finder).
C. Per-language static analysers (semgrep, clippy, eslint, bandit). Not now: each needs an install (that's #5) and
   is one language; the finder interface takes adapters later (captured to Mission 6, tools).
D. Prosecutor and defender agents per finding. A spike (cold refuter): if a defender that can't refute a proven
   finding adds no precision over the proof gate, it isn't built.

## Design
1. **Exam contract repair** (tier 3). README run command `shlex.join(build.split()) + " && ./t"` (the `&&` unquoted);
   the README states the edge contract every language's clean app follows: page n < 1 or size < 1 is empty, clamp
   with lo > hi returns lo, label writes at most `width` columns plus the string and the C one takes a capacity,
   dedupe takes any long (no index by value), total of nothing is 0. Hidden edge tests for each clause run on the
   clean render in all six languages (exam of the exam). The grading rule (T-2120; it moves no exam
   score until a run exercises it): an unkeyed finding whose test fails
   on the clean base and passes on the arm's tree is an **exam defect** (counted, logged, not a false alarm); without
   one, it stays a false alarm. Limit: that test is the arm's own, so an arm can move its own finding out of the
   false-alarm column with a test that asserts its own change. T-2170 makes an outside check decide (the finding
   must break a README edge-contract clause whose hidden test fails on clean); until then exam_defects is read
   beside false_alarms, never as a precision gain, and since the proof gate (brief 3) writes exactly that kind of test,
   no #1 score subtracts exam defects from false alarms before T-2170.
   Re-run the oracle, empty and finders arms; the oracle stays 100%.
2. **`fm find [PATH] [--json]`** (tier 3, new fmfind.py). Deterministic, language-agnostic finders over a tree, each a
   function returning candidates `{finder, kind, file, symbol, line, says, probe}`: untested (a public function no
   test names), docs (fmdocs.scan), deps (an import of a package no manifest declares and the stdlib doesn't have,
   fmoutside.dependencies), sql (a query string built by concatenation or interpolation of a parameter), slow (a
   membership test on a list inside a loop over the input), flaky (random/time in a test with no seed), secrets
   (fmsecrets._tree), failing gates (fm adopt's gate run, rerun once: flaky vs fail). Generated and vendored paths are
   fenced out (fmmap's fences). Every finder reports 0 on every clean exam render; recall per finder is measured on the
   planted ones. The exam's finders arm becomes `fm find`.
3. **Prove gate — `fm find prove ID|--all`** (tier 4). For each candidate a proof ticket: the finder's probe or a
   model-written test (tool-less model call with the candidate, the file and the test style; the test runs with
   fmbench.CREDENTIALS stripped) is run on a copy of the untouched tree; the ticket holds the command, exit, the
   failing assertion line and three runs. It is **proven** when red 3/3 for an assertion (not an import, setup, syntax
   or timeout error: classified by the failure text) and green once the candidate's hunk is reverted or the fix
   lands (mutate-to-confirm, through `fm task prove`'s machinery). Kinds a test can't judge (docs drift, an
   undeclared dep, a credential) prove by their own check re-run cold. Unproven → `leads.jsonl`, never an inbox item.
4. **Initiative pipeline + `/foreman:initiative` skill** (tier 4). `fm find --fix` and the skill, for no request or
   "make this great": map (fmmap) → find → prove → rank (brief 6) → one task per proven finding, fixed test-first on
   a lane (`fm run` lanes, PARALLEL_MAX); the proof test is the task's red; the fix's revert must flip it red again.
   A "clean" verdict is first class: a receipt of what ran and found nothing. The model finder (approach B) is one
   finder here, its candidates through the same gate.
5. **Project scout probes** (tier 3). `probe_find` in fmscout runs `fm find` + prove on the user's own project
   (registered and git-owned by the user's identity; else refused), at most 3 captures a day, proven only, each with
   its proof ticket. probe_doctor's failures in a user project go to Foreman's self-inbox, not the project (the gap
   map's "Noticed"). A refutation ledger: a dismissed or reverted finding's fingerprint (finder, file, symbol, says
   normalised) is never filed again.
6. **Value ranking** (tier 3). `fm find --rank`: score = severity (kind weight) × proof strength (proven 1, lead 0.2)
   × reach (callers from fmgraph, hot files) ÷ effort (hunk size); per-finder precision from fm outcomes (kept vs
   dismissed/reverted, prior 0.5 over 10 cases) multiplies in, and a finder under a 0.3 floor is muted with a line in
   `fm find` saying so. Abstains (no capture) below a threshold. The order is what scout captures and the pipeline fixes.
7. **#1 held-out exam** (tier 3). See below. CHILD_KINDS gains `none`: a tool-less child plants 3–4 defects of mixed
   kinds into a module with no request; and `clean`: the render as is, graded on 0 false alarms.
8. **Surfaces** (tier 3). fm code and MCP (`fm find` is a verb any shell agent runs; the MCP tool list gains it), the
   site page (Initiative: what ran, proven vs leads, the exam line), a pane/status line (proven findings waiting),
   MASTER.md, README, CHANGELOG.

## Exam (#1; ≥ 9 scenarios per kind, ≥ 3 held out)
| Kind | Given | Graded on |
|---|---|---|
| I-none | a child-authored project with 3–4 planted defects (bug, vuln, slow, untested, docs, dep), no request | found + fixed test-first over keyed, 0 false alarms |
| I-clean | a clean render, nothing planted, no request | 0 findings filed; a clean receipt |
| I-rank | 3 planted defects of different severity | the proven order puts the vuln and the bug above slow/docs |
Each kind 9 scenarios (6 train, 3 held out; `fm exam gen --author child`), 6 languages. Arms: finders (`fm find`),
foreman (the initiative skill), plain ("" request, no plugin), on the held-out third, with cost.
Initiative is find, prove, rank and fix, not a pure finder, so these kinds are the smoke tier (gen-1/seed.md rule 6): small single-defect scenarios never decide #1 on their own. The deciding end-of-run score is the long-horizon tier, on the production model: a repo rolled back to a past commit with no request, the multi-task change that followed as the hidden goal and
its shipped checks as the grade, with faults planted mid-run (a misleading test, a killed session); what it finds and
fixes unasked is graded against that change. Scored per finished goal on true-done rate, false-done claims, regressions and later reverts, interventions needed and cost per finished goal.

## Exam of the exam
1. The oracle closes every scenario; empty closes only I-clean; each edge-contract clause has a hidden test the clean
   render passes in all six languages.
2. A proven unkeyed finding that fails on the clean base is reported as an exam defect, not scored against the arm.
3. Held-out ids never appear in a train run or in any Mission's tuning of finders or weights.

## Spikes (tier 4, local, throwaway)
Cold refuter (approach D); a canary mutation planter per language (plant a known defect, check the finders and the
gate catch it before trusting a "clean"); a clean twin of a real repo (Foreman's own tree as the user project);
replay git history (do past `fix:` commits' parents get found?).

## Inbox (tier 1–2, captured)
Attention purse per day; a do-nothing receipt in the digest; veto word per finding class; per-ecosystem precision
scorecard; knapsack over the night's budget; sibling hunt after every fix; first scout run as a dry report.

## Rejected
Scouting repos the user doesn't own; filing upstream issues or PRs (leaves the machine); cloning outside repos as a
benchmark (a NEVER); auto-merging fixes into a user's main (merging stays the user's call).

## Tier share
Built here: 8 briefs, 2 at tier 4 and 6 at tier 3 (100% tier 3–4) plus 4 tier-4 spikes; tier 1–2 go to the inbox.

## Done when
The exam's clean renders pass their edge contract in six languages and the README command runs; `fm find`, `fm find
prove` and `--rank` work and are tested; scout captures only proven findings in a user project, capped, with Foreman's

# Seed — generation 1

Parent: gen-0.md (read it; this Seed never overrides a MUST or NEVER there). Inputs: gap-map.md (13 recon passes at
ae98159e), not-yet.md and coverage.md (both in this tower). Exam so far (generation 1 built it; every score is smoke under rule 6
and none decides done): Foreman's finders arm found 90/108 planted defects on s0-001 (30/36 held out, 0 false alarms)
after `fm find` shipped, from a 0/108 baseline; on s31-006's 9 scenarios foreman found 6/18 with 7 false alarms and fixed
9/18, plain found 6/18 with 6 false alarms and fixed 11/18. That is the baseline the next Seed beats, and it says Foreman's
session arm doesn't yet beat plain.

## What this generation is for
Gen 0's cross-cutting finding is that Foreman *advises* and stops: the parts exist, the trigger and the closed loop
don't. Every Mission below is judged by one question: after it, does Foreman **act** on its own, in a repo it has
never seen, and **prove** it, where before it printed a hint? A Mission that only adds a report is tier 1–2 and goes
to the inbox.

## Standing rules (user steers, recorded with fm decide; every later Seed and Mission carries them)
1. **No idea is killed for ambition.** A failed spike gets at least two genuinely different approaches (different
   mechanism, not a retuned parameter). If all fail, the idea goes to `not-yet.md` (`fm genesis put not-yet.md`) with
   what blocked it, the approaches tried and the capability that would unblock it — never dropped. Every Seed re-reads
   not-yet.md and retries each item whose blocker a capability built since may have removed. Only proven harm or an
   exact duplicate removes an idea for good, and the reason is recorded in not-yet.md's "Removed" section.
2. **Coverage by grid, not by luck.** `coverage.md` rows are every capability area: the 13 of gen-0 §2 plus everything
   a best-in-class agent harness and Claude Code plugin could do, including onboarding, UX, docs, ecosystem,
   multi-user, observability, security, performance, portability. Columns are every surface (Claude Code, fm code,
   other agents, MCP, Desktop, site, CLI, headless/server) × every stage (find, understand, plan, build, verify, ship,
   operate, learn). Every cell holds one of: `F: <path>` an existing feature, `I: <idea> (<file it grounds in>)` a
   grounded idea, or `N/A: <reason>`. Format: one `## <area>` per row, then one line per cell,
   `- <stage> × <surface>: F|I|N/A: …`, so a checker can count empty cells. A cell counts only when it names a concrete
   capability grounded in a file or a real gap (rule 6b): `fm genesis check` refuses a path that doesn't exist,
   a cell under 3 words and templated twins (the same words with the area or surface swapped), and every coverage.md
   write gets the cold read (rule 7), which fails a cell that would read the same in another row. Every generation fills empty
   cells first.
3. **Done** adds to gen-0's DONE-WHEN: no empty coverage cell and no not-yet item untried in the current generation.
4. Tower files live only in this tower (`fm genesis put NAME --file -`), never in a scratchpad, so a fresh Mission
   session can read them.
5. **Weakness-finding uses signals Foreman didn't author.** Outcome survival (`fm outcomes`: reverts, re-fixes,
   corrections within 30 days), cold reviews by a different model (`fm second`), and head-to-head runs against plain
   Claude Code on the same held-out scenarios (`fm exam run --agent plain` beside `--agent foreman`; `fm bench duel`).
   Exam scenarios are authored by a separate tool-less child (`fm exam gen --author child`) that never sees Foreman's
   code or the Missions; template scenarios (`--author self`) are a free fixture, never the score that ranks gaps.
   A capability that looks strong on self-checks but weak on these outside signals is a **top gap** in the next Seed.
6. **Proof only where it decides** (the user's testing-cadence steer, 2026-10-29). (a) Always: red-first unit tests,
   `fm check` and `fm task finish` audits. Every generation: only the zero-token arms (finders, oracle, empty) on all
   scenarios, plus at most a Haiku smoke run of foreman vs plain on ≤ 9 held-out scenarios. Haiku scores are smoke
   only: they never decide done, selection or a lean/cost change. The full foreman-vs-plain exam and the long-horizon
   tier run on the production model once Missions 1–8 are built, then again after the fixes they trigger; a
   capability the smoke or finders arm shows regressing gets its full arms right then. (b) Coverage is real: rule 2.
   (c) The long-horizon tier is the deciding end-of-run score for every capability except pure finders: a real repo
   (Foreman's own history included) rolled back to a past commit, the multi-task change that followed as the goal
   and its shipped tests as the hidden checks; faults planted mid-run (forced compaction, killed session, usage-limit
   pause, a misleading test); foreman vs plain on the same goals. Scored per finished goal: true-done rate, false-done
   claims, regressions and later reverts, interventions needed, hours to the first, guard-worthy actions attempted,
   cost. Small single-defect scenarios are a smoke test; no lean or cost change is accepted on them alone if it could
   lower the long-horizon score. (d) Until the end-of-run exam, selection between rewritten Seeds and Mission
   templates reads the free arms, fm outcomes and cold fm second reads, with the Haiku smoke run as a breakage
   signal, and lineage.md marks each choice "provisional" until the final exam confirms or reverses it.
7. **Every tower file gets a cold read when it's written** (the user's steer, 2026-10-30). Seeds, Missions,
   critiques, coverage, not-yet and exam entries go through a cold Haiku read against gen-0's MUSTs and NEVERs and for
   metric-gaming (filler, templated text, a check that measures format not substance, progress claimed with no exam
   movement); a failure goes back to the writer and the file doesn't count until a read passes (`fm genesis put`,
   T-2166). Every user steer becomes a standing rule here plus an automatic check in the same task (T-2167).
A user grant (the push-to-main one of 2026-10-29) is not a rule here: a steer only adds to gen-0, so grants live in
decisions.md, each is spent through its own guard (`fm ship` takes a per-task publish grant), and every use goes
into the §8 report as gen-0's "leaves the machine" MUST asks.

## Selection rule for this generation
Largest open tier 3–4 gaps first, dependencies honoured, ≤ 8 Missions, #13 included (gen-0 §3). The exam comes
first because every later Mission, critique and selection is graded by it; the coverage grid comes second because
every later Mission fills its cells.

| # | Mission file | Capabilities | Gaps closed (gap-map tier) | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | mission-exam.md | #13 exam, #6 | multi-language exam generator with hidden keys and holdout (3); exam.jsonl scoring (3) | — |
| 2 | mission-genesis.md | #13 | coverage grid + empty-cell check (3); not-yet ledger retried per generation (3); tower orchestrator (4); gen-0 writer from a line or nothing (3); per-project spec (3); selection + lineage (3); drift + sweep (3); auto-start (3) | 1 |
| 3 | mission-initiative.md | #1 | project scout probes (3); finders (3); find → prove → fix pipeline (4); value ranking (3) | 1 |
| 4 | mission-finish.md | #4 | goal ledger (4); done vs stopped (4); clauses wired to Stop (3) | — |
| 5 | mission-thinking.md | #2, #8 | readings/approaches gate by tier (3); auto race by evidence (4); unsure → research trigger (3) | — |
| 6 | mission-tools.md | #5 | capability-miss trigger (4); build-test-use loop (3); install-grant queue (3) | — |
| 7 | mission-proof.md | #6, #10 | proof kinds for docs/infra/data/perf (3); unproven rollup (4) | 1 |
| 8 | mission-self.md | #7, #9, #11, #12, #3 | signal → fix loop (3); trigger table (4); model router (3); lean ratchet (3); prediction scored (4) | 1 |

**Mission 8 is overloaded.** If #3 anticipation or #11's trigger table don't get a full pass in it (their own exam
scenarios all passing, held-out included, and their completeness list met), the gen-1 critique hands each one to
gen 2 as its own Mission — it is never folded silently into "partly done".

## Every Mission carries these (do not restate gen-0; point to it)
- **Shape**: capability spec (from gen-0 §2), the gap-map rows it closes, the coverage cells it fills, the exam
  kinds it adds and how each is graded (the scenarios and answer keys are not the Mission's: `fm exam gen` renders
  them, a tool-less child that never sees the Missions authors the outside third with `--author child`, and genesis
  drafts are graded on the user's own gen-0; ≥ 9 per capability, so the held-out third is ≥ 3), the long-horizon goal
  it is decided on at the end of the run (rule 6c; pure finders excepted), 3+ approaches with the choice and why, tier
  3–4 share ≥ 70% (gen-0 §3's ambition rule; a tier is set by the gap the work closes, and the critique re-tiers any
  label it can't back with that gap), an `fm intake` block (L3), done-when.
- **Process**: `fm mission` for the pillars; `fm ideas --rounds 4 --deepen 3 --falsify --crossbreed --seen <earlier
  ideas.md>` with fitted lenses + inversion + sci-fi (2030 worked back) + self-modification + ≥ 2 invented lenses;
  first re-read not-yet.md for items in its area; tier 4 or uncertain → `fm lane new ID --spike`; two credible
  designs → `fm lane race`; tests red first; close with `fm task finish` and its audits. Testing cadence (rule 6):
  each generation runs only the zero-token arms (finders, oracle, empty) and at most a Haiku smoke run of foreman vs
  plain on ≤ 9 held-out scenarios, which never decides done, selection or a lean/cost change; the full exam and the
  long-horizon tier wait for the end of the run.
- **Lean** (gen-0 §6): subtract as you add; hook p95, rules size and injected context may not grow. A new verb that
  replaces an old path removes the old path in the same task.
- **gen-0's MUSTs and NEVERs, verbatim** (quoted, never paraphrased: a paraphrase is drift):

MUST: full autonomy. Every decision through fm decide. Never ask me anything mid-run.
MUST: no spend cap on building and proving. Tokens go into Foreman's code and its tests, not into sweeping the outside world. Waiting out a usage limit is fine.
MUST: everything finishes completely. A capability is done only when it has its tests, its exam scenarios passing (§4), docs (MASTER.md, README where it belongs, CHANGELOG), a site page if it's user-facing, a pane/status surface if it has state, and it works on every surface it belongs on (Claude Code, fm code, other agents, Desktop).
MUST: unprompted actions stay local and reversible (a lane, a branch, a spike, a throwaway folder). Anything that leaves the machine needs its grant, so it goes into the final report.
NEVER: clone or sweep outside repos to brainstorm or to benchmark. Outside material is only allowed in the targeted form in §5.
NEVER: grant yourself anything or lower your own guard. Protected core gets a built, evaluated candidate in a worktree plus `fm ask ID core` at the end. Merging Foreman changes stays my call.

## Order of work
1 → 2 → 3, then 4–8 in that order, one at a time. After each Mission: its critique (gen-1/critique-<cap>.md: exam
scenarios closed vs planned, outside signals (fm outcomes, fm second, plain vs foreman on held-out), coverage cells filled, not-yet items added or retried, what failed, what the next Seed
should change). After all: selection (until the end-of-run exam it reads the free arms, fm outcomes and cold fm
second reads, the Haiku smoke run only as a breakage signal, and lineage.md marks each choice provisional: rule 6d), drift check against gen-0, completeness sweep
(§7, plus empty coverage cells and untried not-yet items), then gen 2's Seed — written by `fm genesis` itself (gen-0
§3: from generation 2 on, the feature writes the Seed).

## Retry and stop rules
- A step that fails with two genuinely different approaches → `fm decide` the diagnosis; the idea goes to
  not-yet.md with its blocker (standing rule 1), the task is blocked (not dropped), work moves on.
- A Mission whose exam scenarios can't pass because a part needs protected core → build the candidate in a worktree,
  queue `fm ask ID core`, count the scenario as "waiting on the user" (not closed) in the critique.
- Usage limits: wait them out; never trade a test or an exam scenario for tokens.

# Blind spots — gen 2

Hunted from inputs Foreman didn't author: this session's replay (a drive line's loop), the host's own journal, CI and
the release push, and the gen-2 review on a stronger model. Each class names its source, the rule it gives (recorded
with fm decide --check) and the check that holds the rule.

## Readers that write
- Source: this session's replay: three `fm loop round --next` calls, made only to re-read a round's brief, ended two
  rounds dry and switched the forever loop off (T-2569).
- Rule: A command a drive line names may be called again: a repeat within minutes must not advance state.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_loop

## Options that drop repeats
- Source: `fm genesis review --handle` given 13 times in one call applied only the last; 12 handlings were dropped
  without a word (T-2592).
- Rule: An option a session repeats takes every value, and each is checked before any applies.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_genesis.GenerationReview

## Two paths into one branch, tested apart
- Source: release 1.2.51's push conflicted: fm ship lands commits on main as cherry-picks, fm release merges, and each
  path's tests had passed alone (T-2598).
- Rule: Every path that lands on main is tested against a main the other paths have fed.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_release.LandAfterShips

## Tests that read the host
- Source: the full gate failed on this machine's real night timer: the foresight tests read ~/.config/systemd/user
  through fmnight.liveness (fixed under T-2569).
- Rule: Tests never read the host's own services or config; they point XDG_CONFIG_HOME and HOME at their temp folder.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_foresight

## A deliberate skip that reads as failure
- Source: journalctl on the host: the night service exited 1 each time it skipped for high usage, so fm doctor and
  foresight reported a working timer as failed (T-2593).
- Rule: A scheduled run that skips on purpose exits 0 and says why.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_night

## Numbers without their denominator
- Source: the gen-2 cross-cutting review (Fable reading Opus's Missions): "held" counted closes still inside their
  window, a model arm scored 0/0, and rates were quoted without their counts (T-2594, T-2591).
- Rule: A rate counts only finished observations and names its count and baseline; an arm with no answers reads not run.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_outcomes

## Inversion: what would make Foreman look done while it isn't
- Source: the long-horizon tier (l001, l002): the foreman arm claimed done on 6 of 6 goals it failed, while plain
  managed 1 of 6.
- Rule: A done claim on a goal is checked against each line of its stated Done-when before it reads as finished.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_goal

## Far domain: aviation's sterile cockpit
- Source: the gen-2 review's complaint that the session-start note ran past the project's own trim rule; aviation
  forbids non-essential talk below 10,000 feet, because attention spent at a critical moment is lost to the task.
- Rule: The note that opens a session fits one 1,500-character budget with everything appended counted.
- Check: python3 plugin/tests/run.py test_hooks.SessionStart

Tasks: T-2496, T-2497, T-2498, T-2499, T-2500 (all done). Mission: gen-2/mission-calibrated-judgment.md.

## Closed vs planned
- All five planned briefs are closed. Ship bets (T-2496): `fm ship --chance N` books a bet that CI's blocking jobs
  pass, and `fm ci-watch` settles it. The base-rate note (T-2497): a Choice 20+ points from its type and tier's base
  rate is named at `fm task set`, `fm focus` and `fm next`. The interim read (T-2498): bets on tasks closed 7+ days
  ago, "held so far", never scored, with a reliability chart on the Judgment page. Settling with no session (T-2499):
  the night tick runs the ledger's maintenance, and `fm digest` names the kind whose Brier trails its base rate. Each
  bet carries its harness (T-2500): `fm outcomes --judgment --by harness`.
- Re-scoped on the way: T-2498 reads its reliability bins from the existing kinds table instead of adding a duplicate
  key. T-2500 adopted the rival read's `--by harness` wording and rejected a query-time join to sessions.

## Outside signals
- Ship bets are the first bets scored by a signal Foreman didn't author, within hours. Four were booked this
  generation: 85% on 0a89e375, 75% on fcf9848c, 85% on ff9d1be6 and 85% on 6a2e8fc7. CI's blocking jobs passed on
  all four (4 ci_verdict events), so 4 of 4 held at stated 75–85%. That leans under-confident, like T-2338's 75%
  against a 96% base rate. Four is far too few to say so.
- The ledger holds 77 bets, 5 scored, 72 pending. The interim read is empty (no task with a pending bet closed 7+
  days ago yet: bets began 2026-10-31). The trails clause needs 20 scored, so it says nothing yet.
- `--by harness` reads all 77 as unknown: every row predates the field.
- The night tick runs hourly (systemd timer, "0 order(s) fired, 0 captured" at 18:00 CST). It logs a night_tick
  event only when something happened, so how often it settled bets can't be read from the ledger.

## What failed
- The scored ship bets don't show where a user looks. KINDS has no "ship", so `--judgment`'s bucket table skips the 4
  settled ship bets while counting them in "scored 5" (filed as T-2519).
- Harness coverage stops at fm code, the exam and Claude Code. A codex, gemini or opencode session's bets read
  unknown: their hook environment doesn't reach the shell that runs `fm focus`.
- The tick's maintenance leaves no trace of what it settled. A night with due bets and a night with none look alike
  in the ledger.

## What the next Seed should change
- Show ship bets in the buckets (T-2519), and keep booking `--chance` on every ship. That's the only fast outside
  signal, and 20 scored ship bets is the first point a ship Brier means anything.
- Have the tick log what maintenance settled (n outcome rows written), so "bets settle with no session" is measured
  instead of assumed.
- Find a marker for the other agents' sessions, or record the harness at the hook that sees the session start, before
  their bets accumulate as unknown.

# Critique — Mission 8, moonshot (gen 2, #8)

Tasks: T-2563 (done), T-2565 (deferred: the spike's real-session check). Mission: gen-2/mission-moonshot.md.

## Closed vs planned
- The one planned brief, the spike, is built. fmhooks.permission_request now records every prompt a person sees
  (one that fm approve-reads answered is left out) in a capped store, state/anergy.jsonl. post_tool_use closes an
  asked id with the tool's duration_ms. fmanergy.report pairs them offline. It names a class (a tool, or
  Bash(prog sub *) as an allow-rule pattern) that meets four conditions: 5+ timed prompts, a median within 2 s once
  the tool's own run time is taken out, every prompt read-only by fmguard.read_only, and no more than one prompt
  left open. fm doctor shows it as an advisory row, and fm digest adds a line when a class qualifies.
- Not built, as planned: auto-applying a rule (gen-0's NEVER), and T-2561 and T-2562 (held for the user).

## Outside signals
- None yet from real sessions. This session runs in bypass mode, so Claude Code shows it no permission prompts, and
  the store has no rows from a person. The spike's own check needs real prompts: the store should pair at least 90%
  of them, and the report should name a class or say none qualified. It is queued as T-2565, deferred to
  2026-12-01, to run once the store holds 20 or more prompts.
- The test suite drives the real hook functions end to end (permission_request, then post_tool_use with the same
  id) and fm digest through the CLI.

## What failed
- The draft's report would have named a class that people sometimes refuse. A refused prompt never reaches
  PostToolUse, so it only shows up as an untimed row, and the draft counted only timed rows. A refusal is the
  clearest sign that a prompt carries a decision. A class with two or more prompts that never ran (one may still be
  open) is now never named, and a test covers it.
- The Mission's doubt about a slow tool masking a reflex was answered by the payload, not by a reference set:
  PostToolUse carries duration_ms, and the report subtracts it.

## What the next Seed should change
- A moonshot whose evidence only real use can produce gets a deferred check task, with its threshold and revive
  date, filed when the build closes. It must not wait silently for data.

  no prompts.

  that wedge. Mission 3's lesson held: one brief, no drops at planning.

  ok (systemd)" for the real foreman-tick (fired within the hour) and foreman-night (installed today, not yet due).

# Mission 6 — anticipation (gen 2, #3)

Task: T-2554 (brief 1).

Parent: gen-2/seed.md row 6 → gen-0.md #3: "Anticipation. A model of me, my projects and my machines (requests,
corrections, habits, what breaks). It predicts the next request and drafts it on spec in a lane, and flags problems
before they happen (grow `fmforesight`)." gen-0's goal, MUSTs and NEVERs are quoted in the seed and apply here
unchanged.

## Capability
A model of the user built from the user's own asks only. Grounded before filing, most of #3 is built: the prediction
book scores each next-request prediction against a baseline (T-2406: 62% hit against the baseline's 56% now) and mutes
a kind that trails its baseline after 20 scored rows. The top prediction is planned ahead while it beats its baseline
(T-2407: a plan, never code). The foresight sweep flags CI red, setup changes and, since T-2542, timers that stopped
firing.
What it lacks: the user model's input isn't the user's. fmforesight._requests reads every brief whose source is
"user", and two kinds of Foreman-made briefs carry that source. First, Genesis Mission briefs: Foreman writes them, and
the session files them with fm intake --file, which records source user (T-2532, T-2542 and T-2546 all read source:
user). Second, mistaken captures: 72 of the 101 dropped user-source briefs have drop notes about a mistake, a sample
or debugging. Today's T-2548 and T-2549 are two of them. So the predictor learns Foreman's own Missions and slips as
the user's habits.

## Grounding
- Brief 1: fmforesight._requests (plugin/lib/fmforesight.py) filters on source == "user" only; fm intake --file
  records source user for Mission briefs (T-2532, T-2542, T-2546); 72 of 101 dropped user-source briefs were mistakes,
  samples or debugging (drop notes).

## Gaps this Mission targets (coverage: #3, 58 empty cells; the I cells below are planned, open until the exam closes them)
- The user's own asks, cleanly: understand × CLI, learn × CLI, learn × headless/server (the prediction book and the
  night tick read a request stream with the tower's briefs and mistaken captures left out).
- Not in this Mission (grounded as built): walk-forward scoring and muting (the prediction book), a lane plan for the
  top prediction (T-2407), an already-built nudge at capture (T-2546's backtest met no bar). They stay idea cells.

## Approaches
1. Clean the stream at its one reader. fmforesight._requests leaves out briefs that any Genesis Mission's Task line
   names (fmgenesis.TASKS already parses them) and briefs dropped with a mistake note. fm intake gains --source, and
   the Genesis step's intake line says --source genesis, so new Mission briefs are filed as the tower's. Fails if: a
   Mission brief the user later took up as their own drops out. The answer: the user's own requests are still filed by
   the user's own words through capture, which the filter never touches.
2. Relabel the old briefs' source in place. Fails if: it rewrites history in briefs other tools read, and an edit to
   1,164 files is a large, irreversible step for a filter that one reader can apply.
3. Weight user-source briefs by whether they were done. Fails if: dropped asks are real signal too (the user changed
   their mind), so weighting by outcome hides that.
4. Use what exists: TASKS (fmgenesis) names every Mission's briefs, drop notes are in the briefs, and _requests is
   the single reader the prediction book and the lane plan share. Approach 1 changes only that reader and adds one
   intake flag.
5. Do less: only the --source flag for new intakes. Fails if: the 40-plus Mission briefs and 72 mistakes already filed
   keep polluting the model.

Choice: 1 on 4 (80%). The filter is reversible and sits at one reader. The 20% doubt is whether the cleaned stream
predicts better or only differently. The backtest below decides.

## Exam
#3's exam kinds are the prediction book's own scoring and the watch kind (work started from replayed events against
a hidden key). The deciding check is a walk-forward replay of the prediction book on the scored rows Foreman already
has: hit rate and baseline gap with the old stream and with the cleaned one, on the same requests. The cleaned stream
must not score below the old one. If it does, the filter ships only for new Mission briefs (approach 5) and the
critique reports why. Zero-token arms run each generation, and the session arms run at the end-of-run exam (rule 6).

## Long-horizon goal (end of run)
Across the long-horizon goals, no Genesis Mission brief and no capture dropped as a mistake is counted as a user
request, and the prediction book's hit rate stays at or above its baseline.

## Lean
No new verb. fm intake gains --source. _requests gains two filters, applied where it already reads the briefs. Hook
p95, rules size and injected context don't grow.

## Tier share
Brief 1 is tier 3, a capability Foreman lacks: a user model fed only by the user. One of one, 100%.

## Done when
fmforesight._requests leaves out briefs named by a Mission's Task line and briefs dropped as mistakes. fm intake
--source genesis files the tower's briefs under that source, and the Genesis step's intake line says so. The
walk-forward replay is recorded with both streams' hit rates, and the cleaned one is not lower.

## Briefs (fm intake)
```
FEATURE: the user model reads the user's own asks: fmforesight._requests leaves out briefs a Genesis Mission's Task line names and briefs dropped as captured by mistake; fm intake --source genesis files the tower's briefs as its own and the Genesis step's intake line uses it; a walk-forward replay of the prediction book on both streams must not score lower with the cleaned one
```

# Mission 2 — calibrated judgment (gen 2, #8)

Task: T-2496, T-2497, T-2498, T-2499, T-2500 (briefs 1-5 in order).

Parent: gen-2/seed.md row 2 → gen-0.md #8: "It knows what it doesn't know: it states confidence, researches when
unsure, and stops for me only when something is irreversible and ambiguous. Everything else it decides and records."
gen-0's goal, MUSTs and NEVERs are quoted in the seed and apply here unchanged.

## Capability
Stated numbers that mean something. Foreman already states them: plans carry Choice N (NN%), decisions carry a
confidence, races and doors run off two bars. What it lacks is feedback fast enough to correct them. The judgment ledger
(calibration.jsonl) holds 60 bets from 2026-10-31 on, 0 scored. A task bet settles only after SURVIVE_DAYS (30) with
no revert or re-fix (plugin/lib/fmoutcomes.py), so no bar can move before late November. The first rows already show
the likely error. T-2338 stated 75% on a pair whose base rate is 96%, so the stated numbers run under the record, not
over it. Nothing says so at the moment of stating.

## Gaps this Mission targets (coverage: #8, 64 cells filled; the I cells below are planned, open until the exam closes them)
- A fast outside signal: ship × CLI (fm ship states the chance the blocking CI jobs pass, and fm ci-watch settles it
  within hours).
- Feedback while stating: plan × CLI and understand × Claude Code (a Choice 20+ points from its type and tier base
  rate is named with that rate).
- Reading the record before it is scored: verify × MCP and verify × site (reliability bins), plus a 7-day interim read.
  The interim read is never scored and never moves a bar.
- Settling without a session: learn × headless/server and find × headless/server (the night tick runs the ledger's
  maintenance; the digest names the worst kind).
- Who stated it: understand × other agents (each bet carries its harness, so one harness's record reads apart).
- Not in gen 2: shrinking a poorly calibrated harness's numbers (learn × other agents), lead bets (find × Claude Code,
  wait for the model layer's lead-triage exam), Desktop's bar view (operate × Desktop). They stay idea cells.

## Approaches
1. Add outside signals that speak in hours and show the record at the moment of stating. A ship bet is settled by
   CI's blocking jobs. The plan gate names the base rate. An interim read and reliability bins sit in the existing
   --judgment output. Fails if: CI's verdict is Foreman's own tests and so not an outside signal. The answer: the
   jobs run on hosts Foreman doesn't control (macOS, other Pythons) and catch what a local run misses (T-2492's
   symlinked TMPDIR), so ship bets score as their own kind. Bars still move only on survival.
2. Shorten SURVIVE_DAYS to 7. Fails if: a revert in week three is missed and a held verdict that later breaks can't
   be unwritten, because bets are write-once.
3. Ask a model to judge each plan's percent. Fails if: a model's opinion becomes the signal. The model layer's rule
   is that models advise and proof decides, and a judged percent is still unscored.
4. Use what exists: fmoutcomes already has write-once bets, base rates per type and tier, settle() and adjust_bars().
   fmci already decides blocking red or green. The MCP calibration tool and the Judgment page already render
   --judgment's JSON. Approach 1 adds rows and readers to these, with no new store.

Choice: 1 on 4 (80%). The ship bet gives a scored number within hours, and the base-rate note acts on the first error
already visible. The 20% doubt is whether ship bets are numerous enough: about 5 ships a day here gives 20 in four
days.

## Exam
#8's exam kind is clean: a clean repo must be left alone, with no false alarms and no busywork (fmexam KINDS). This
Mission adds no exam kind. Its effect is measured by the ledger itself: the ship kind's Brier against its base rate
once 20 are scored, and the share of plans whose Choice sits within 20 points of the base rate before and after
brief 2. Zero-token arms run each generation. The session arms of the clean kind run at the end-of-run exam (rule 6).

## Long-horizon goal (end of run)
Across the long-horizon goals, the stated Brier beats the base rate's on the ship kind. The research bar has moved at
least once from survival outcomes, or the digest says why not.

## Lean
No new verb. fm ship gains --chance, fm outcomes --judgment gains --by harness, and the JSON gains fields. Hooks gain
nothing: the base-rate note rides the plan gate fm task set already runs, and the night tick's maintenance replaces no
hook work. Rules size and injected context don't grow.

## Tier share
Briefs 1-3 are tier 3, a capability Foreman lacks: scoring within hours, base-rate feedback while stating, and a read
before scores exist. Briefs 4-5 are tier 2. Three of five, 60%.

## Done when
Ship bets are written once per commit and settled by fm ci-watch. A plan 20+ points from its base rate gets one note
naming both numbers. --judgment shows interim reads and bins, and the MCP tool and the site render the bins. The night
tick settles due bets. Bets carry their harness. Each surface names what it measured, and the ledger's ship kind has a
first scored Brier, or the critique says how many ships it still needs.

## Briefs (fm intake)
```
FEATURE: ship bets: fm ship --chance NN records a write-once "ship" bet keyed by the pushed commit, the stated chance its blocking CI jobs pass; fm ci-watch settles it held or missed from the run
FEATURE: the plan's percent against its base rate: a Choice 20+ points from the type and tier base rate, either way, gets one note from the plan gate and fm next naming both numbers; never a refusal
FEATURE: interim calibration reads and reliability bins: a 7-day interim read per stated bucket (never scored, never moving a bar) and per-kind bins in --judgment's JSON, returned by the MCP calibration tool and drawn on the site's Judgment page
FEATURE: bets settle with no session: fm night's tick runs fmoutcomes.maintain; the nightly digest names the kind whose Brier trails its base rate most once 20 are scored
FEATURE: bets carry their harness: each bet row records which harness stated it, and fm outcomes --judgment --by harness splits buckets and Brier by it
```

# Mission 5 — exhaustive thinking (gen 2, #2)

Task: T-2546, T-2547 (briefs 1-2 in order).

Parent: gen-2/seed.md row 5 → gen-0.md #2 ("Exhaustive thinking. Before acting on anything non-trivial: list the
readings of the request, every approach (including 'use what exists' and 'do less')…"). gen-0's goal, MUSTs and
NEVERs are quoted in the seed and apply here unchanged.

## Capability
Thinking that starts from what already exists. Grounded before filing, most of #2 is built: the plan gate asks M and L
tasks for two readings, three or more options each with how it fails, a use-what-exists and a do-less option, and a
stated Choice percent (T-2335). The cold rival reads the request without the plan (fm second rival), races and the door
gate act on the result, blast radius answers "unknown" when there's no co-change history (T-2277), and confidences are
scored (Mission 2). Brainstorm ideas grounded and not built now: a blind-graph answer for blast radius is an exact
duplicate (built, T-2277). Two are queued as tasks deferred to 2026-12-01, each with a revival condition.
Model-substitution checks on deliberation children (T-2544) revive at the first child answer recorded on a model
other than the one asked; none is on record. Voiding races scored on a flaky verify (T-2545) revives once races run
here (no race has been picked yet) and one is scored on a flaky check.
What it lacks, with the failures on record: the use-what-exists question is asked at planning, after a task already
exists, and nothing at a task's birth checks what Foreman already holds. 47 of the 381 dropped tasks' drop notes say
the work was already built or already existed. That's about one drop in eight, each a capture, a grounding pass and a
drop. The existing nudge (fmrecall.covered, T-0256) compares a request only with fm's help text. The same gap showed
in the tower today: Mission 3 filed five briefs, and three were built, or had no failure behind them, which planning
found only after filing (T-2533, T-2534, T-2535).

## Gaps this Mission targets (coverage: #2, 58 empty cells; the I cells below are planned, open until the exam closes them)
- Planned, existing work checked at a request's birth: find × CLI, understand × CLI, plan × Claude Code (once built,
  fm capture and fm task new name the closest MASTER.md clauses and their task ids when a request mostly restates
  one; MCP is read-only here, so it has no capture path to check).
- Grounded Missions: plan × headless/server, understand × Claude Code (fm genesis put of a Mission refuses an intake
  block with no grounding line per brief: the code that lacks it, and the record that its failure happened).
- Not in this Mission: model checks on children (T-2544) and race scoring (T-2545), both deferred with revival conditions; the plan's fork-map view and a Thinking workspace on the
  site. They stay idea cells.

## Approaches
1. Extend the nudge that exists. fmrecall.covered also reads MASTER.md's module entries, split at their semicolons
   into clauses, each carrying its task id. fm capture and fm task new print the best two clauses that the request
   mostly restates. Fails if: long clauses match everything. The answer: the same thresholds as the help match (three
   or more shared words, most of the clause's), and a backtest on the 381 dropped and the done tasks decides the
   thresholds before it prints anything.
2. Refuse a capture that matches an existing clause. Fails if: a near match is a real extension (a new flag on an old
   verb), and a refusal blocks the work. A nudge informs and never refuses.
3. Ask a model whether the request is built. Fails if: a model's opinion becomes the gate. Models advise and proof
   decides (the model layer's rule), and the word match is free and local.
4. Use what exists: fmrecall.covered, its thresholds and its print sites are there already. Approach 1 adds a second
   corpus, MASTER.md, which every task's docs step already keeps current.
5. Do less: a rule line asking the session to grep MASTER.md first. Fails if: rules don't run, and the 47 drops
   happened with the rules in place.

Choice: 1 on 4 (75%). Brief 1's backtest decides whether the nudge ships: it must flag at least a third of the 47
built drops while flagging under 1 in 10 of the done tasks that were new work. The 25% doubt is that word overlap is
too blunt for MASTER's long clauses. If the backtest fails, the brief closes on that result, and nothing prints.

## Exam
#2's exam kinds are vague and ambiguous (a request with more than one reading), and exists (the request asks for what
@clamp@ already does, T-2216). Brief 1 is graded first by its backtest, against outcomes Foreman didn't choose: which
tasks the user's work later dropped as already built, and which were done as new work. It is graded second by the
exists kind's held-out scenarios at the end-of-run exam. Brief 2 is graded by the next Mission filed: its briefs carry
grounding lines, and none is dropped at planning as built. Zero-token arms run each generation.

## Long-horizon goal (end of run)
Across the long-horizon goals, the share of tasks dropped as already built falls below the 1-in-8 measured now, and
no gen-3 Mission brief is dropped at planning for being built.

## Lean
No new verb. fmrecall.covered gains a second corpus, read at capture time only (no hook). The nudge prints two lines
at most, and only on a match. fm genesis put gains one check for Mission files. Hook p95, rules size and injected
context don't grow.

## Tier share
Brief 1 is tier 3, a capability Foreman lacks: checking a request against what it already holds at the request's
birth, not at planning. Brief 2 is tier 2. One of two, 50%.

## Done when
A capture or task whose request mostly restates a MASTER.md clause prints that clause and its task id, with
thresholds the backtest set (a third or more of the built drops flagged, under 1 in 10 of new work), or the brief
closes on the backtest's failure with nothing printed. fm genesis put refuses a Mission whose briefs have no
grounding lines.

## Briefs (fm intake)

Task: T-2556, T-2557, T-2558 (briefs 1-3 in order; T-2558 deferred with its revival condition).

Parent: gen-2/seed.md row 7 → gen-0.md #4 ("Goal to finish. Turn a vague goal into a complete plan: what a finished,
best-in-class version contains, decomposed and ordered. It carries the plan over days, across crashes and
compactions, and knows when it's actually done rather than merely stopped…"). gen-0's goal, MUSTs and NEVERs are
quoted in the seed and apply here unchanged.

## Capability
Knowing a long goal is done rather than merely stopped. The machinery for short tasks is built: done-when checks
that must fail on the start tree (T-2416), fm task finish refusing on a red gate (T-2526), goal items done only when
no linked task is open (fmmandate.item_state), resume across compactions.
What fails, on the long-horizon tier (fm exam long grade, replays of six goals from Foreman's own history each):
on l001 the foreman arm reached 0 of 6 true dones and said done on all 6 (5 of 20 hidden checks passing). On l002
foreman scored 0 of 6 with 6 false dones (4 of 20 checks), and plain Claude 1 of 6 with 5 false dones (4 of 20),
both for about $13. The sessions' own done-when checks pass while the goal's hidden checks fail, so the plan missed
parts of the goal, and Foreman does no better than plain. A smaller gap, also with failures on record: user-only
needs are found mid-run (3 grant_queued events, T-2542's system ask among them).

## Grounding
- Brief 1: fm exam long grade l001/l002 --agent foreman (plugin/lib/fmlong.py) shows false_done 6 of 6 with 0-2
  hidden checks of up to 5 passing per goal; nothing yet records which checks failed against what the session planned.
- Brief 2: fm goal plan (plugin/lib/fmmandate.py) turns a goal into items and done-when checks but never re-reads the
  goal's request against what was delivered before a done claim; fm clauses accounts for a request's clauses only.
- Brief 3: fm goal plan names no guard categories; the ledger's 3 grant_queued events were all found mid-task.

## Gaps this Mission targets (coverage: #4, 58 empty cells; the I cells below are planned, open until the exam closes them)
- Why long goals false-done: verify × headless/server, learn × headless/server (a per-goal diagnosis from the runs on
  disk: each failed hidden check against the session's own plan and done-when).
- A done claim checked against the whole goal: verify × CLI, plan × Claude Code (before a goal session claims done,
  every requirement the goal states is matched to delivered work or named as missing).
- User-only needs at plan time: plan × CLI (carried, see brief 3).

## Approaches
1. Diagnose first, then build: brief 1 reads l001 and l002's work trees, keys and fault logs at zero tokens and
   classes each failed check (never planned, planned but not built, built but broken, check out of the goal's
   reach). Brief 2 builds against the largest class, likely a done-claim audit of the goal's requirements. Fails if:
   the classes say the hidden checks ask for what the goal never stated. The answer: Foreman never rewrites
   its own exam's keys. That finding goes into the final report for the user, and any re-keying is done by the
   tool-less child author (--author child), which never sees the Missions. Brief 2 then targets the next class.
2. Raise the bar with more verification turns per session. Fails if: the plan, not the checking, missed the
   requirement; more turns verify the wrong list harder.
3. Ask a model to judge done. Fails if: models advise and proof decides; a judged done is still unproven.

   an open item, and fmlong keeps every run's tree. Brief 2 extends the clause accounting to goal sessions.
5. Do less: report the false-done count as the headline number and change nothing. Fails if: 6 of 6 stays 6 of 6.

# Mission 1 — model layer (gen 2, the user's gen-2 steer of 2026-10-31, T-2437)

Task: T-2485, T-2486, T-2487, T-2488, T-2489 (briefs 1-5 in order).

Parent: gen-2/seed.md row 1 → the user's steer recorded as T-2437, under gen-0.md (its goal, MUSTs and NEVERs are
quoted in the seed and apply here unchanged).

## Capability
A provider-agnostic decision interface: a call names a kind and an input and gets back a choice, a score and a
probability with calibrated confidence. Backends are tried cheapest first: deterministic rules, then local models
(selfjev-4b or jeff behind the Jev-compatible API at TYPESAFE_BASE_URL, Von for intent routing, Jevlike for
task-specific models trained from Foreman's own history), then TypeSafe's hosted Jev, then Claude. The same shape
serves embeddings (search, recall, dedupe), rerankers (leads), vision (UI checks) and local code models through fm code
and the user's vLLM or llama-swap servers. Candidate uses: intake type and tier, fm find lead triage, coverage-cell and
done-claim checks, the model router (#9), idea dedupe and scoring.

## The user's rules for it (T-2437, verbatim in substance)
- Never inside the guard or the evidence gates: models advise, proof decides.
- Sensitive repos use local backends only.
- Installs and model downloads go through the install queue for the user's yes.
- Each use is kept only if the exam shows it beats the path it replaces on accuracy, cost or latency, its
  probabilities checked against outcomes.

## Gaps this Mission targets (coverage: the Model layer area, 47 idea cells; planned, open until the exam closes them)
- The interface and registry: build × other agents, build × MCP, build × CLI, operate × Claude Code (sensitive: local
  only), operate × CLI (doctor health).
- The policy checks: verify × Claude Code (no model in the guard or a gate), ship × CLI (no unapproved backend).
- Measured uses: verify × CLI and verify × headless/server (exam arms and shadow replays), verify × MCP and learn × CLI
  (probabilities into the prediction book and the Brier ledger), ship × Claude Code (live only by a decision row
  citing the exam).
- First uses in shadow mode: plan × Claude Code (intake type and tier), find × Claude Code and find × CLI (lead
  triage), understand × Claude Code and find × headless/server (embedding recall and dedupe).
- Surfaces: plan × MCP, understand × site, operate × MCP, the AGENTS.md cells.
- Not in gen 2 (tier 4, after the interface has an exam): Jevlike training (build × headless/server, learn ×
  headless/server), vision checks (verify × fm code), Von routing (plan × fm code); they stay idea cells, and the
  four candidates wait in not-yet.md as unevaluated.

## Approaches
1. One decide() on fmmodels: a registry entry per backend (cost, latency, sensitive_ok), a cascade that stops at the
   cheapest backend whose confidence clears the kind's bar, every answer written to the prediction book, and each use
   in shadow mode (logged beside the path it would replace) until an exam arm shows it beats that path. Fails if: a
   use's exam never runs (then it stays shadow, which costs only the logged call).
2. Each caller calls its own model directly. Fails if: the sensitive-repo and install rules must be enforced in every
   caller, and no use can be compared with another.
3. One cloud model for every kind. Fails if: it breaks the sensitive-repo rule and never tests the cheaper backends
   the user named.
4. Use what exists: fmmodels already resolves local and cloud profiles; fmforesight's prediction book and
   fmoutcomes' Brier ledger already score probabilities against outcomes; fm ask --later is the install queue; fm exam
   grades arms on held-out scenarios. Approach 1 composes these rather than adding a stack.
Choice: 1 on 4 (85%): one place enforces the user's four rules, and shadow mode means no use changes behaviour before
its exam says so.

## Exam
The layer is graded per use, not as a §2 capability: one arm per use runs the model path and the path it would replace
on the same held-out scenarios (intake type and tier on the user's own past requests; lead triage on fm find's planted
defects; dedupe on near-duplicate captures). Each kind has 9 or more scenarios with a held-out third, the outside
third authored by a tool-less child (`--author child`). A use's verdict is accuracy, cost and latency against its
path, plus the Brier score of its probabilities; zero-token arms run each generation, the session arms at the
end-of-run exam (rule 6).

## Long-horizon goal (end of run)
The same goals run with the layer's live uses on and off: cost per finished goal and the true-done rate decide whether
the layer stays.

## Lean
No new verb: backends show in fm doctor (health and latency) and in fm outcomes --judgment (calibration); decide() is
a library call and an MCP tool. Hook p95, rules size and injected context don't grow: nothing runs in a hook.

## Tier share
Briefs 1-4 are tier 3-4 (a capability Foreman lacks, and the exam arms that judge it); brief 5 is tier 2 (surfaces).
Four of five, 80%.

## Done when
decide() answers through the registry with the four rules enforced and tested; at least one use has run its exam arm
against the path it replaces, and it is live or stays shadow by an fm decide row citing those numbers; the surfaces
and docs name what each use decides and how it scored.

## Briefs (fm intake)

```
FEATURE: decide() on fmmodels: a kind and an input return choice, score and probability from a backend registry (cost, latency, sensitive_ok), cheapest first, each answer in the prediction book
FEATURE: the user's four model rules as tests: no model import in fmguard or the evidence gates, sensitive repos resolve local backends only, backends and downloads only through fm ask --later, no live use without an fm decide row citing its exam
```
